newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt prices stumble on worries over Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt prices stumble on worries over Yeltsin.

text.p: Worries that President Boris Yeltsin's health may be worse than thought scared off some investors on Wednesday, sending Russian debt prices to their lowest for a month.

Kremlin doctors said the 65-year-old Russian leader, recovering from a quintuple heart bypass only to be hit by pneumonia last week, was improving but his illness was serious and warned of possible complications.

The news knocked half a point of Vneshekonombank paper, the actively traded foreign commercial debt which Russia inherited after the collapse of the Soviet Union and which is close to being restructured.
"We really need more information. That fact that it is serious is what we have been assuming since last week," one debt trader said.
The price of the debt fell to a little over 77 cents in the dollar, well below the high of 82 cents last October.
Moscow is in the final stages of turning some $32 billion in arrears to Western banks into new loans with repayments stretching out to 25 years.
Russia was the star performer on the emerging debt market last year, with prices surging 150 percent.
Analysts and traders have been prediciting more, albeit less spectacular, gains this year with the Russian economy expected to show growth for the first time since the Soviet Union broke up.
Many also believe the country has changed enough for its programme for sweeping economic reform to stay on track and that it is not longer so dependent on the fate of one leader.
Some are less worried by the prospect of an early election -- Yeltsin was re-elected last summer -- than of an ailing Yeltsin lingering in office but barely able to carry out his duties.
Until the issue of his health becomes clearer, traders said prices are bound to remain volatile.
"With Russian debt at the moment, you have got to be fairly agile and not take too long a view," one trader said.
